title: Pilot telemetry quiet-window and rollback playbook sync
summary: Weekly POC sync to review pilot telemetry baseline, define a quiet-window approach for phased rollouts, agree canary thresholds and rollback playbook. Agreed on smoke tests, dashboards to ship, and next steps for a short high-load run and a DR rehearsel.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-07 16:00 UTC | Duration approx 54m
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Laura (Redwood SE), Anita (Nimbus Head Platform), Ben (Nimbus SRE), Cara (PM), Jordan (ML Eng)

00:00 Samir: hi everyone, thanks for joining, we're hoping to use this slot to finalize the quiet window definition and the rollback playbook for pilot cutover. quick roll call?
00:12 Anita: Anita here, sorry I'm on mobile for first bit.
00:15 Ben: Ben, SRE.
00:17 Cara: Cara, product.
:19 Jordan: Jordan, ML eng.
00:21 Samir: great, laura from my side?
00:23 Laura: hi all, Laura Gomez, I'll run through telemetry gaps and proposed dashboards.

02:05 Laura: quick context recap — last week we saw elevated tail latency spikes during shopping cart bursts, around 500ms p50 to p95 spread, and KV cache hits weren't as high as expected. There's a hypothesis that the prefix caching config needs tuning for your 256-token average prompts.
02:30 Ben: yeah that matches our logs, we also caught a few OOMs on the smaller quantized instance type when we hit sustained 45 QPS.
02:40 Samir: ok noted. for rollout approach we proposed earlier the quiet-window where we route a small steady percentage and watch telemetry without automated rollbacks, vs a strict canary which actively gates traffic based on SLOs. today's goal: pick the primary approach and codify the thresholds + rollback steps.

04:18 Jordan: i'm leaning on a hybrid. start with a quiet-window for 24 hours to validate telemetry and then flip to a canary for ramp. quiet-window reduces blast radius but may not show rare edge failures.
04:44 Anita: agree, also our compliance team wants an audit trail of all rollbacks and decisions — SSO and audit-ids need to be captured.

06:10 Laura: dashboard plan: central panel for p50/p95/p99, token throughput, kv cache hit rate, GPU util, error rate 5xx and model errors. we'll add a small table for request samples that trigger longer generates. suggested canary thresholds: p95 < 700ms, error rate < 0.5% for 30m window. if either breaches, amber alarm; if sustained 30m amber then auto-fallback to smaller model variant and alert on-call.
06:45 Ben: amber then auto fallback — who owns execution? do we let Redwood initiate fallback in hosted or do we play manual?
06:53 Samir: for Dedicated you can choose automated fallback; for Private we recommend semi-automated steps. For this pilot (dedicated pool) Redwood can program the fallback but we'll require an explicit owner to approve final cutoff. proposal: Redwood triggers the fallback to the compatible smaller model variant and notifies Nimbus SRE; Nimbus SRE can trigger full cutover rollback to baseline if needed.
07:20 Cara: what's the expected performance delta when we fallback to smaller model? that impacts UX.
07:28 Laura: about 25-40% latency improvement on high tail, but lower quality on complex prompts. we'll capture examples in the request samples table.

09:05 Jordan: we should define a quiet-window length and success criteria. I propose 24 hours with a 15-minute rolling window for the alarms — enough to catch repeating regressions.
09:22 Samir: sounds reasonable. what about traffic fraction for quiet-window? earlier we suggested 5% steady traffic with no AB weighting.
09:30 Anita: 5% seems low, will it surface caching effectiveness? maybe 10% for 6h then down to 5% for longer.
09:40 Ben: 10% for initial 6 hours, yes — that'll create realistic prefix reuse patterns.

11:00 Laura: noting telemetry gaps: request sampling is at 1% currently so we need to bump to 5% during the quiet-window and 10% during the high-load trial so we have representative inputs. also we need to ship a JVMM-style trace link for slow requests — we can attach request-id to Redwood logs.
11:25 Samir: we'll add the sampling config change to the runbook and make it reversible. I'll send a runbook PR link: https://redwood.in/sync/runbooks/nimbus-quiet-window (placeholder).

13:10 Ben: rollback playbook specifics — step 1: detect (alarm), step 2: automated fallback to smaller model variant, step 3: run smoke test traffic, step 4: if smoke test fails, full rollback to baseline cluster and route all traffic back, step 5: postmortem. need roles and SLAs for each step.
13:40 Samir: agreed. propose timings: detect -> fallback within 2 minutes, smoke test run within 5 minutes, decision to fully rollback within 20 minutes of failed smoke tests.
13:55 Cara: who runs smoke tests? our SREs or Redwood SE automation?
14:00 Laura: Redwood can run the smoke test automation via the playbook endpoint (we'll provide script). Nimbus SRE must confirm results within the 5m window.

16:20 Jordan: small thing — ensure not to clear KV cache on fallback; otherwise cold starts explode. Instead fall back to model variant that shares KV format.
16:34 Laura: yep the runtime supports KV compatibility between those variants, we'll mark compatible images in the runbook.

18:50 Anita: compliance ask — log retention for audit trail, can we increase to 180 days for this pilot?
19:00 Samir: yes, we can toggle retention for the pilot trial; there might be fees for extended retention, I'll include cost note in the PR.

21:10 Ben: monitoring alerts — integrate into our PagerDuty. Also want Slack channel prefix #nimbus-pilot.
21:20 Samir: we'll push alerts to your PD and create the channel webhooks. Laura will share the alert specs.

23:50 Cara: walk me through an example failure path, like sudden token regen storm.
24:00 Laura: if token regen storm occurs we'll see token throughput spike, GPU saturation, p95 rises. Alarm triggers amber state. Redwood fallback kicks in moving 10% or more of requests to smaller model, then smoke tests to validate. If smoke fails — full rollback. We'll document exact metric expression in the runbook.

27:15 Jordan: can we do a rehearsel — DR run — where we intentionally create a simulated failure and run the rollback?
27:25 Samir: yes, recommended. schedule a rehearsal in next two weeks during off-peak. propose 2026-05-18 for rehearsal window.
27:40 Anita: works for us. add to calendar.

29:50 Laura: on observability dashboards: will export a CSV of flagged requests every 6 hours for the pilot. Also will add a simple diff view comparing baseline and pilot model outputs using a token-level quality score.
30:15 Cara: quality score — what's the threshold for human review?
30:22 Laura: if quality delta > 8% on evaluation set then flag for product review. We'll attach the eval set link: https://redwood.in/evals/nimbus-eval (placeholder).

32:40 Ben: action item — we need a short runbook checklist for preflight: network rules verified, KMS keys present, SSO/RBAC configured, PD and slack endpoints, smoke test script committed.
32:58 Samir: I'll craft a compact preflight checklist and share.

35:10 Cara: timeline recap? when do we flip to quiet-window and the high-load trial?
35:18 Samir: proposed dates: quiet-window start 2026-05-10 00:00 UTC for 24-48 hours with initial 10% for 6 hours then 5%, then 2026-05-13 run high-load 6h trial at 60% to validate autoscaling. Rehearsal rollback on 2026-05-18.
35:40 Anita: approved pending cost estimate.

38:00 Laura: last bit — sample retention and request-id mapping needs to be consistent. Also ask Jordan to provide top 50 prompt patterns so we can craft targeted smoke tests.
38:15 Jordan: will share CSV by Monday.

40:22 Samir: ok let's do a quick recap of next steps and owners.
40:30 Ben: quick interrupt, competitor note — BigCloudAI has a managed fallback feature but it doesn't do KV-compatible fallbacks, saw some nasty cold-starts.
40:45 Samir: noted, I'll put that in competitor column.

42:00 Recap (rough):
42:05 Samir: 1) Runbook PR with retention/cost notes (Samir)
42:12 Laura: 2) Dashboards + alert specs + increased sampling during quiet-window (Laura)
42:20 Jordan: 3) Share top 50 prompt patterns + eval corpus (Jordan)
42:28 Ben: 4) SRE to confirm network/KMS/PD hooks (Ben)
42:35 Cara: 5) Product to approve trial dates (Cara)
42:40 Anita: 6) Schedule rehearse rollback 2026-05-18 (Anita + Samir)

48:30 Samir: any other Qs?
48:40 Anita: one compliance Q: will audit logs include who initiated fallbacks?
48:47 Laura: yes, we'll include audit-id and actor in the event logs.
48:55 Anita: great.

52:00 Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the PR and a short confluence page. Expect runbook link and dashboards by EOD Friday.
52:12 Cara: thanks all.
52:20 Meeting end.

Anita & Samir: schedule rollback rehearsal for 2026-05-18 and invite participants
